introduction: Today, fifty days after Easter, we celebrate Pentecost. The Holy Spirit comes upon the disciples like a mighty wind and tongues of fire, and they proclaim the mighty works of God in every language. Paul tells us that there are many gifts but the same Spirit, given for the good of all. In the Gospel, the risen Jesus breathes on the disciples and says, Receive the Holy Spirit. With Pentecost, the Easter season ends. Come, Holy Spirit.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God has given us his Spirit, who renews the face of the earth. Let us bring our prayers to the Father.
intentions: For the Church throughout the world: that the Holy Spirit may make her one body in Christ, rich in many gifts. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who were confirmed this year: that they may use the gifts of the Spirit for the good of others. Let us pray to the Lord.
For peoples divided by language, culture or conflict: that the Spirit may bring understanding and peace. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who need forgiveness: that they may receive it through the ministry Jesus gave his Church. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may be sent by Christ as he was sent by the Father. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Father, you poured out your Holy Spirit on the Church at Pentecost. Renew in us the gifts of your Spirit, and send us out to bear witness to your Son. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Receive the Holy Spirit
reflection.body:
Pentecost was a Jewish feast fifty days after Passover, and Jerusalem was full of pilgrims from many lands. The disciples "were all with one accord in one place" when "there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind." Tongues like fire rest on each of them. "They were all filled with the Holy Spirit," and the crowd hears them speaking "in our languages the mighty works of God!" The Church is born, and from its first day it speaks to all nations.

Paul tells the Corinthians that the Spirit is the source of every gift in the Church. "No one can say," Jesus is Lord, "but by the Holy Spirit." And the Spirit gives different gifts to different people: "Now there are various kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit." Each gift is given "for the profit of all." Like the parts of a body, we are many but one: "For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body."

In the Gospel, John tells of another gift of the Spirit, on the very evening of Easter. Jesus appears to his frightened disciples, gives them his peace, and sends them: "As the Father has sent me, even so I send you." Then "he breathed on them, and said to them," Receive the Holy Spirit! The first gift he entrusts to them is the forgiveness of sins.

The breath of Jesus recalls the breath of God at creation, when he breathed life into the first human being. Pentecost is a new creation. The psalm prays: "You send out your Spirit and they are created. You renew the face of the ground."

Today the Easter season ends, but the Spirit's work goes on in us. This week, ask yourself what gift the Spirit has given you, and how you can use it for others. And pray every morning: Come, Holy Spirit.
